docs.title: Python Course Project
docs.text:
The final project is Учебная платформа, a learning platform with a versioned FastAPI backend. The API guide covers authentication, course and lesson management, automatic test grading, sequential learning, progress, personalized practice, migrations, and deployment.

The final project is split into review branches, with the complete implementation on DEV-7. Homework solutions are preserved on the remote ASSIGNMENT-4 and ASSIGNMENT-6 branches.

Start with the Developer quickstart to set up the workspace, run a FastAPI service, and check your first change.

This is a uv workspace with independently scaffolded services and libraries. Use just new-service api and just new-lib common to create members and regenerate the README tables. No repository is needed to start locally.

just check services/api checks one member in its own environment. just check checks all members and the separate integration scope. Member pytest configuration discovers only its tests/ and measures its src/. Edit templates/readme/*.jinja for workspace documentation and run just codegen. Member READMEs contain direct badge links and remain editable.

See Development tools for the testing stack, each tool's purpose, and setup requirements for API, database, and browser tests.

GitHub CI uses independent member jobs. See CI reports for Pages layout, Allure history, and the one-time PR that binds README and template badges and deletes its workflow and binding script. Dependabot maintains generated project dependencies weekly.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
checks.yml is shared by default-branch and pull-request workflows. It discovers services/*/pyproject.toml and libs/*/pyproject.toml for a dynamic job matrix, including an independent integration job even when there are no members. fail-fast: false lets healthy members finish when another fails collection. A separate tooling job checks the generated README and builds documentation.

Pants owns the dependency graph and CI target selection. Each member scaffold includes a BUILD file covering its Python sources, tests, and other files. Pants infers first-party dependencies from Python imports. uv continues to own package installation and its lockfile; Just runs the existing lint/test commands. For runtime relationships that cannot be inferred from imports, add an explicit dependency such as libs/common:member to the consumer's python_sources target in its BUILD file. Manifest declarations alone do not create Pants graph edges.

PR discovery runs pants --changed-since=<merge-base> --changed-dependents=transitive list and converts its target addresses into unique member paths with jq. Integration always runs. Member metadata/assets are dependencies of that member's Python targets; shared configuration, lockfiles, and tooling are dependencies of all members. Deletions and renames run the full matrix because a removed import may no longer have an owner in the current graph. Default-branch publication also checks every member, keeping published reports and Allure history complete.

Install the Pants launcher for local queries; pants.toml pins the engine version. CI installs it in discovery. There is no generated dependency graph or dependency regeneration command:

pants dependencies --transitive services/api:member
pants dependents --transitive libs/common::
pants --changed-since=HEAD --changed-dependents=transitive list

See Pants target selection for native filters and changed-file options. PRs build Allure reports for selected scopes only; unselected members have unavailable results in the combined artifact.

The same Just commands run locally and in CI:

just check services/api
just test libs/common
just lint integration
just check
just reports

Each member's pytest invocation runs from its directory, installs its declared workspace/runtime dependencies and shared dev tools into .venvs/<group>/<name>, and measures only its own src/. The shared uv lockfile still resolves the whole workspace. Separate environments expose imports of unrelated workspace packages; they do not prevent access to transitive or tooling dependencies.

Integration tests use a separate environment with all members installed. Their coverage does not contribute to member badges. Empty integration suites are allowed; empty member suites fail. Root scripts and integration tests are linted under the integration scope, along with the shared root conftest.py. Members run their own lint and formatting checks.

Native Ruff, pytest, coverage, and Allure outputs go directly to each scope's report directory. build_reports.py only summarizes those outputs; it neither runs checks nor partitions workspace-wide results. Missing results/tool errors show unavailable, empty suites show no tests, and skipped suites show skipped. Reports are published after failing checks when report generation succeeds; the checks keep their failure status. PRs retain artifacts without publishing.

docs.title: Browser failure videos
docs.text:
Integration, service, and library pytest configurations enable --video=retain-on-failure. Tests using pytest-playwright's managed browser fixtures record videos; passing-test recordings are discarded. Install the browser before running UI tests, for example uv run --group dev python -m playwright install chromium. Linux CI also needs playwright install --with-deps chromium and the application under test running. Tests that do not use a browser do not launch one.

Raw videos live under reports/<scope>/playwright/<test>/. The root conftest.py attaches finalized WebM files to the corresponding failed Allure test, including setup or teardown failures when a recording exists. Member pytest configurations set --confcutdir=../.. to load this shared hook while retaining their own test and coverage settings. No per-test attachment code is needed.

Allure copies attachments into reports/<scope>/allure-results/; the existing artifact and Allure report jobs retain them. just test <scope> clears that scope's old videos and Allure results before running. Override recording when needed with PYTEST_ADDOPTS='--video=off' just test <scope>. Contexts created manually outside the pytest-playwright fixtures need their own recording setup.

This follows the Allure pytest-playwright video guide, with attachment after the teardown report so pytest-playwright has finished retaining its artifacts. Attachment errors are logged without replacing the test's original failure.

docs.title: Badge setup
docs.text:
GitHub Pages is configured with GitHub Actions as its source at https://alexxios.github.io/python-course-project/. The README and scaffold templates already use this URL for their badges and report links. The one-time setup workflow and binding script were removed after configuration.

Default-branch CI publishes the documentation and reports. Badges become available after the first successful deployment. No custom token or secret is required.

Future just new-service and just new-lib commands render direct links from the bound templates without Git/network access or a saved URL configuration. Running Cookiecutter directly on either member template works the same way. The setup preserves member prose and updates only standalone Shields lint, tests, and coverage badge lines. Normal codegen never rewrites member READMEs.

After a Pages/domain move, update the plain report URLs and URL-encoded Shields endpoints in existing member READMEs, templates/service/*/README.md, templates/lib/*/README.md, and templates/readme/header.md.jinja, then run just codegen. Shields needs public access to the endpoint JSON.

docs.title: Published layout
docs.text:
/
├── index.html                         MkDocs documentation
├── ci-reports/                        This guide
└── reports/
    ├── index.html                     Links and status for every scope
    ├── services/<name>/
    │   ├── index.html                 Only this service's check results
    │   ├── badges/{lint,tests,coverage}.json
    │   ├── coverage/                  Only its source, from its tests
    │   ├── allure/                    Its Allure report and trends
    │   ├── allure-results/            Native results and attachments
    │   ├── playwright/                Retained browser failure videos
    │   ├── history.jsonl              Published Allure history snapshot
    │   ├── junit.xml
    │   ├── coverage.xml, coverage.json
    │   ├── ruff.json, ruff-format.json
    │   ├── lint.exit, format.exit, test.exit
    │   └── summary.json
    ├── libs/<name>/                   Same layout for each library
    └── integration/                   Separate integration results

Pages deployment uses an Actions artifact; no gh-pages Git branch is needed. Coverage pages exist only when data is available. Every badge opens its own member's report, which links to its coverage and Allure pages.

docs.title: Allure history
docs.text:
The reporting job restores .allure-history/ from a default-branch cache and builds an Allure report for each scope using a separate <scope>.jsonl history file. It then saves the histories using a unique run/attempt key. Failed test runs still enter history. Default-branch workflows are serialized to avoid competing history updates. Cache eviction starts new history.

PRs build Allure reports without restoring or saving history. Each scope's artifact is uploaded even if its checks fail; the reporting job collects them into check-reports and, on the default branch, the Pages artifact.

docs.title: Учебная платформа: API v1
docs.text:
The final project implements theme 5 from the course brief: a backend for a learning platform. All business endpoints are under /v1. Interactive docs are at /v1/docs, ReDoc at /v1/redoc, and OpenAPI at /v1/openapi.json.

Follow the quickstart for SQLite development or the PostgreSQL Docker Compose stack. The review stack ends at DEV-7. Assignments 4 and 6 remain on their dedicated remote branches.

docs.title: Requirements and implementation
docs.text:
Brief requirement Implementation Course catalog Public, published courses; title search and pagination Course, lesson, and test data model SQLAlchemy models, foreign keys, constraints, and Alembic migration User registration and authentication Student registration, login, bearer sessions, refresh rotation, password changes, logout Administrator CRUD Separate course, lesson, and question endpoints under /v1/admin Sequential course completion Enrollment and prerequisites checked for every lesson read, completion, and test submission Previously learned content Completed lessons remain accessible for revision Automatic test grading Server-side answer validation, score calculation, passing threshold, and attempt history Personal cabinet Current profile, enrolled courses, completion percentages, and private grades Personalized test generation Local adaptive question selection and optional AI generation from completed lessons Deployment Existing Dockerfile plus Compose files in infra/ with shared PostgreSQL and migration startup dependency Testing Endpoint, authorization, persistence, migration, property, and OpenAPI tests

Optional video links are supported on lessons. Teacher accounts and course reviews are not part of this implementation; course authoring uses the administrator role specified in the backend requirements.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All bodies and results are JSON. Public registration always creates a student; clients cannot choose their role. Provision an administrator using the CLI:

uv run --package app python -m app create-admin --username admin --first-name Admin --last-name User

The command prompts for a password. For noninteractive provisioning, supply it through LEARNING_ADMIN_PASSWORD in the command's environment. Existing accounts are never silently promoted or overwritten.

curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"username":"student","first_name":"Иван","last_name":"Ли","password":"a unique long example password"}'

curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"username":"student","password":"a unique long example password"}'

Login returns access_token, refresh_token, token_type: "bearer", and expires_in in seconds. Send Authorization: Bearer <access_token> for protected requests. Swagger's Authorize button accepts the access token directly.

Usernames contain 3–50 ASCII letters, digits, or underscores and are normalized to lowercase. Names are required. Passwords contain 12–128 characters and are stored using Argon2id. Tokens are cryptographically random opaque values; only SHA-256 token digests are stored in the database. Responses never contain password hashes. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes and refresh tokens after 7 days by default. ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS and REFRESH_TOKEN_SECONDS configure those limits.

Refresh tokens are single use: refresh replaces both tokens and invalidates the old access token. Logout revokes the current token pair. A password change checks the current password and revokes every session; log in again afterward.

Method Path Request / purpose POST /v1/auth/register username, first_name, last_name, password; returns 201 POST /v1/auth/login username, password; returns a token pair POST /v1/auth/refresh refresh_token; rotates the token pair POST /v1/auth/change-password current_password, new_password; returns 204 POST /v1/auth/logout Revoke current session; returns 204 GET /v1/me Current user's public profile

docs.title: Administrator API
docs.text:
Every /v1/admin operation requires an administrator access token. POST returns 201, GET and PUT return 200, and successful DELETE returns 204. Updates use full PUT bodies; omitted optional fields take their defaults.

Resource Collection operations Individual operations Courses GET/POST /v1/admin/courses GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/admin/courses/{course_id} Lessons GET/POST /v1/admin/courses/{course_id}/lessons GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/admin/lessons/{lesson_id} Questions GET/POST /v1/admin/lessons/{lesson_id}/questions GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/admin/questions/{question_id}

A course starts unpublished. Create it with title, optional description, and passing_score (1–100, default 70). Add lessons before publishing it through PUT /v1/admin/courses/{id} with published: true. Course lists accept an optional published filter.

A lesson has title, description, nonempty text content, positive position, and optional HTTP(S) video_url. Positions are unique within the course and need not be contiguous. A lesson's test consists of its ordered question records.

{
  "prompt": "Which Python collection is mutable?",
  "options": ["list", "tuple"],
  "correct_option": 0,
  "position": 1
}

Questions have 2–6 distinct options, a zero-based correct_option, and a unique positive position within the lesson. A lesson supports at most 100 questions. Only administrator responses contain answer keys.

Once anyone enrolls, course settings, lessons, and questions cannot be edited or deleted (409). Create a new course revision instead. This keeps prerequisites, grades, and completion history consistent. Before enrollment, deletions cascade through dependent lesson/question records. Unpublish a course before deleting its last lesson.

docs.title: Student API and learning rules
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose GET /v1/courses Public published catalog; search, limit, offset GET /v1/courses/{course_id} Public course description POST /v1/courses/{course_id}/enroll Enroll current user; returns 201 and progress GET /v1/courses/{course_id}/lessons Enrolled user's lesson outline with unlocked/completed flags GET /v1/lessons/{lesson_id} Accessible lesson content and questions without answer keys POST /v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/complete Complete a lesson without a test, or return existing completion POST /v1/lessons/{lesson_id}/attempts Submit and grade all questions; returns 201 GET /v1/me/courses Paginated enrolled courses with progress GET /v1/me/courses/{course_id}/progress Progress and next lesson for one enrollment GET /v1/me/attempts Private grade history; optional course_id and lesson_id filters

Only the catalog and public course descriptions are anonymous. Enrollment is required to see lesson content. The first lesson is unlocked immediately; all earlier lessons must be complete to access a later lesson. The outline never exposes locked content. Completed lessons remain accessible.

Submit exactly one selected option for every question in the lesson:

{"answers": [{"question_id": 1, "option": 0}]}

Missing, extra, duplicate, or out-of-range answers return 422 without recording an attempt. Valid answers produce correct_count, question_count, score, and passed. Score is the percentage of correct answers, rounded to two decimals for display. Passing uses the exact ratio against the course threshold. A passed test automatically completes the lesson. Failed tests can be retried; every valid attempt is retained. A later failed retry does not revoke an earned completion.

The completion endpoint cannot bypass a required test. Completion is idempotent. Progress is calculated as completed lessons divided by the total, not accepted from client input. Separate users have separate enrollments, completions, and grade histories. Duplicate enrollment returns 409.

Paginated collections return {items, total, limit, offset}, with default limit 20, maximum 100, and stable ordering. Resource IDs and offsets are bounded by the database's signed 32-bit integer range. The curriculum is returned as an ordered outline. Grades and practice quizzes are listed newest first.

docs.title: Personalized practice
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose POST /v1/me/practice-quizzes Generate with course_id and question_count (1–10, default 5) GET /v1/me/practice-quizzes Current user's paginated practice history GET /v1/me/practice-quizzes/{quiz_id} Retrieve a private quiz POST /v1/me/practice-quizzes/{quiz_id}/submit Submit one answer per generated question

At least one lesson must be completed. Generated questions use their own IDs within the practice quiz and identify a source_lesson_id. Answer keys remain server-side. A quiz can be submitted once; generate another for a retry. Practice scores do not modify course progress or replace required lesson tests.

QUIZ_GENERATOR=local is the default and needs no external service. It selects questions from completed lessons, prioritizing lessons with lower average test scores, then course order. It returns up to the requested number when fewer questions are available, or 409 if completed lessons have no questions. This is adaptive question-bank selection, not AI generation.

For new AI-generated questions, configure:

export QUIZ_GENERATOR=openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY='your-api-key'
export OPENAI_MODEL='your-compatible-model-id'

Choose a model available to your account that supports Responses structured outputs. The integration uses the OpenAI Responses API with Structured Outputs. Only titles, IDs, and text excerpts from completed lessons are sent (up to ten lessons and 2,000 characters per lesson). Identity, credentials, and grades are not sent; provider response storage is disabled. The generator validates answer options, requested count, and source lesson IDs before storing anything. Unconfigured AI returns 503; timeout, refusal, malformed output, or a question referencing unlearned material returns 502. It does not silently switch providers. AI questions may be imperfect and are used for revision, not official grading.

docs.title: Data, migrations, and deployment
docs.text:
The nine application tables are users, auth_sessions, courses, lessons, questions, enrollments, completions, attempts, and practice_quizzes. alembic_version tracks migrations. All timestamps are UTC Unix seconds. Foreign keys are enabled in SQLite as well as PostgreSQL. Writes use request-scoped transactions that commit before a response is sent or roll back on failure.

Migrations are packaged with the service and run with python -m app init-db. The API never automatically creates or upgrades a schema. See the quickstart for the Compose stack in infra/. In Kubernetes, provide the learning-platform Secret with a database-url key and run the services/app/k8s/migration-job.yaml job with the same release image before rolling out the deployment. Set the job image as well as the Kustomize image; the standalone job is not part of the deployment's Kustomization.

Readiness requires database access and an initialized user table. Liveness stays independent of the database. Application errors use 401 for invalid credentials, 403 for permissions/prerequisites, 404 for missing or private resources, 409 for conflicts, and 422 for input validation. Database failures return 503 without exposing SQL, credentials, or connection paths.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
just check
just check services/app
HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=fuzz just test services/app

Tests cover every endpoint, authentication and role boundaries, refresh replay and expiry, password change revocation, CRUD, frozen enrolled courses, sequential access, grading, progress, privacy, migrations, and AI validation. All AI calls in tests use RESPX mocks; no key or paid request is needed. Hypothesis checks grading properties; Schemathesis generates catalog requests. Reproduce a reported seed by running the relevant module from services/app/:

uv run --package app pytest tests/integration/routers/v1/test_learning.py -m fuzz --hypothesis-seed=<seed>

Unit tests under services/app/tests/unit/ cover package metadata and pure grading logic, with mocks or patches for external dependencies. Integration tests under services/app/tests/integration/ cover API, OpenAI provider, database, migration, CLI, and concurrency behavior using PostgreSQL Testcontainers.

Both suites mirror directories under src/app/. Tests for a single source file are named test_<filename>.py: routers/v1/auth.py maps to tests/integration/routers/v1/test_auth.py, and learning.py maps to tests/unit/test_learning.py. Database/client fixtures live in tests/integration/conftest.py; shared API factories live in tests/integration/routers/v1/conftest.py. Module-specific fixtures live in the corresponding test file.

Run both suites with just test services/app. From services/app/, select one with uv run --package app pytest tests/unit or uv run --package app pytest tests/integration. Select a handler with, for example, uv run --package app pytest tests/integration/routers/v1/test_auth.py -k refresh.

Integration tests require a running Docker daemon. Testcontainers starts one PostgreSQL container per session and removes it afterward. The image is read directly from services.postgres.image in infra/docker-compose.yml, keeping the test database version aligned with the development infrastructure. Each test and generated API fuzz example uses its own schema, applies migrations, and drops that schema afterward. The suite includes refresh-token row-lock concurrency and HTTP responsiveness while a PostgreSQL query waits for a lock. CI uses the same fixtures; no separately configured database service is needed. Unit tests do not require Docker, and the development Compose stack does not need to be running for integration tests. Coverage, JUnit, and Allure output for both suites go under reports/services/app/. The separate root tests/ scope remains available for workspace-level integration tests and reports under reports/integration/.

docs.title: Async operations
docs.text:
The API uses SQLAlchemy AsyncEngine and per-request AsyncSession transactions. SQLite runs through aiosqlite; PostgreSQL uses psycopg async connections. Existing sqlite:///... and postgresql+psycopg://... URLs remain valid. Database queries and readiness checks are awaited, and shutdown awaits disposal of the connection pool. Alembic migrations use AsyncConnection.run_sync. Password hashing and verification run in worker threads. Pure grading and response projection remain synchronous computations.

Tests use AnyIO's asyncio backend and HTTPX AsyncClient. The application, fixtures, requests, and pooled connections share a single event loop per test. Each request/task gets its own session. Blocking SQL and password regression tests verify that liveness remains responsive while those operations are pending.

AI requests use HTTPX AsyncClient; a regression test checks liveness while a provider response is pending. No live provider calls are made in tests.

docs.title: Developer quickstart
docs.text: The selected final-project theme is Учебная платформа. The business API and interactive documentation are versioned under /v1. Earlier homework solutions remain on the ASSIGNMENT-4 and ASSIGNMENT-6 branches.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Install Python 3.14+, uv and Just, then run from the repository root:

uv tool install rust-just
just bootstrap
uv run pre-commit install
uv run --package app python -m app init-db
uv run --package app python -m app create-admin --username admin --first-name Admin --last-name User
uv run --package app uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload --reload-dir services/app/src

The administrator command prompts for a password of 12 to 128 characters. No default administrator is created. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/docs, call POST /v1/auth/login with your username and password, and paste the returned access token into Authorize. Use the administration endpoints to create a course, its ordered lessons, and test questions, then publish the course.

Register a separate student with POST /v1/auth/register, log in as that student, enroll in a published course, and progress through its lessons. The API guide describes every endpoint and the grading rules.

The default database is learning.sqlite3 relative to the current working directory. It is excluded from Git and Docker build contexts. The application does not create tables on startup: run init-db before serving requests. The command applies packaged Alembic migrations and is safe to repeat.

To choose an absolute SQLite path or PostgreSQL, export DATABASE_URL before running both the migration and the server:

export DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////absolute/existing/directory/learning.sqlite3
# Or connect to your PostgreSQL database:
# export DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://app:app@127.0.0.1:5432/app
uv run --package app python -m app init-db

The SQLite parent directory must exist. CLI/server settings come from process environment variables; .env is used by Docker Compose, not loaded implicitly by the Python application. just bootstrap creates .env from .env.example only when it is missing.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Start Docker Engine or Docker Desktop, then run from the workspace root:

just bootstrap
docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml up --build -d api
docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml ps -a
docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml exec api \
  uv run --no-sync python -m app create-admin --username admin --first-name Admin --last-name User

infra/docker-compose.dev.yml adds the API and migration service to the shared infrastructure in infra/docker-compose.yml. The command builds the existing service Dockerfile, starts postgres, waits for database health, runs migrations, and starts the API. The migration container exits successfully after applying the schema. PostgreSQL is also available on 127.0.0.1:5432 for host development; set POSTGRES_PORT in .env to change that port. The API binds to 127.0.0.1:8000 by default; set APP_PORT to change its port. Database data persists in the shared postgres-data volume.

POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, and POSTGRES_PASSWORD default to app for local development. Override them in .env before the first startup. Use URL-safe credentials (letters, digits, _, -) with this local Compose template, which interpolates them into the connection URL. Omit the final api from the startup command to include Redis, Prometheus, and Grafana in the same stack. See infra/README.md for connection and monitoring settings, and for notes on data from the previous root Compose stack.

Inspect logs or stop the combined stack with the same Compose files:

docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml logs api migrate
docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/docker-compose.yml -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml down

The database volume is retained when the stack is stopped.

docs.title: Check the service
docs.text:
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/live
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/courses
just check

Liveness reports whether the app can respond. Readiness checks the lifecycle and database schema access, returning 503 before migration or during a database outage. The catalog initially contains no courses.

just check validates generated documentation, builds MkDocs, runs Ruff, and executes pytest in isolated member environments. Each scope emits coverage, JUnit, and Allure artifacts under reports/. just check services/app checks only the API service. Start Docker before running the app's integration tests; Testcontainers manages a disposable PostgreSQL container using the same image as infra/docker-compose.yml. See tests for integration and fuzz runs.

docs.title: Daily workflow
docs.text:
just format
just check

Keep runtime version bounds in the root pyproject.toml. Declare dependency names and extras without bounds in consuming members, and commit the shared uv.lock alongside manifest changes. Edit templates/readme/*.jinja for the generated workspace README and run just codegen.

just new-service <name> and just new-lib <name> still scaffold workspace members. App unit tests live in services/app/tests/unit/; API and database tests live in services/app/tests/integration/ and use PostgreSQL Testcontainers. just docs, just serve, and just reports retain the existing documentation and reporting workflows. See Development tools and CI reports for the shared tooling.

docs.title: Final project review branches
docs.text:
The learning platform is split into six cumulative branches. Review each branch against its immediate predecessor so its diff contains only that feature. DEV-1 and the assignment branches are existing work and are unchanged.

Branch Review base Scope DEV-2 main (ab14799) Application/database foundation, models, initial migration, health checks, v1 routing, removal of the old appeals example DEV-3 DEV-2 Registration, login, rotating sessions, logout, password changes, profile, administrator CLI DEV-4 DEV-3 Administrator course/lesson/question CRUD, published catalog, content freeze after enrollment DEV-5 DEV-4 Enrollment, sequential lessons, completion, grading, progress, private attempt history DEV-6 DEV-5 Personalized practice, local generation and optional AI provider DEV-7 DEV-6 PostgreSQL Compose, Kubernetes migration job, complete API and development documentation

Each feature branch includes its own async implementation and tests. DEV-2 adds async engines, migrations, lifecycle handling, and database regression tests. Later branches await their database operations; authentication offloads password work and practice awaits provider HTTP calls. The published foundation commit remains in history, with async support added as a follow-up commit.

The shared database schema and dependency lock are introduced in DEV-2; subsequent branches enable their respective routes. All business routers live under src/app/routers/v1/, with the /v1 prefix registered once in that package. Infrastructure probes stay in routers/health.py at their existing URLs.

App tests are split into services/app/tests/unit/ and services/app/tests/integration/, both mirroring the directories in src/app/. API integration tests for routers/v1/auth.py live in tests/integration/routers/v1/test_auth.py, while unit tests for learning.py live in tests/unit/test_learning.py. Integration fixtures provide temporary PostgreSQL schemas and accounts isolated per test, using Testcontainers with the database image configured in infra/docker-compose.yml.

# Inspect one review unit.
git diff DEV-3...DEV-4

# Work with the complete project.
git switch DEV-7
just check

# Run only the refresh handler tests.
cd services/app
uv run --package app pytest tests/integration/routers/v1/test_auth.py -k refresh

Merge in numerical order, targeting each review at the base in the table. After its predecessor lands, retarget the next review to main. The original unsplit implementation is preserved locally on backup/final-project-before-split (9391a7c). No remote history is rewritten.

The previous synchronous review stack is preserved locally on backup/before-async (c4a0351).

docs.title: Development tools
docs.text: Run just bootstrap to install the shared dev and docs dependency groups from the workspace's pyproject.toml. The testing tools are available in each member's isolated test environment and in the integration environment.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Testing type Tools Purpose Unit / integration pytest + HTTPX (pytest, httpx) Run tests and fixtures; exercise FastAPI through its HTTPX-based TestClient, or use AsyncClient with ASGITransport for async API tests. API fuzzing Schemathesis (schemathesis) Generate requests from FastAPI's OpenAPI schema to find server errors, schema violations, and unexpected behavior. Edge cases / property testing Hypothesis (hypothesis) Generate inputs and shrink failing examples. Define strategies that express the constraints of your Pydantic models, including custom validation rules. Mocking outbound APIs RESPX (respx) Mock outgoing synchronous and asynchronous HTTPX requests, control responses, and assert calls without contacting external APIs. Database integration Testcontainers (testcontainers[postgres,redis]) Start real PostgreSQL and Redis containers for tests. Requires Docker; your application's database driver determines whether connections are async. Browser end-to-end Playwright + pytest-playwright (playwright, pytest-playwright) Test browser workflows with isolated browser fixtures. Playwright offers sync and async APIs; the included pytest plugin provides sync fixtures and failure video capture.

The app keeps isolated unit tests in services/app/tests/unit/ and PostgreSQL integration tests in services/app/tests/integration/. Mock or patch external dependencies in unit tests. Both suites mirror directories under src/app/; tests for one source file are named test_<filename>.py. Workspace-level integration tests belong in the root tests/ directory. Run them with:

just test services/app
just test integration
just test

From services/app/, use uv run --package app pytest tests/unit or uv run --package app pytest tests/integration to select one suite.

For async API tests, use @pytest.mark.anyio with HTTPX's AsyncClient and ASGITransport. AnyIO is installed through HTTPX; set the anyio_backend fixture to "asyncio" when the application uses asyncio drivers. Manage the application's lifespan explicitly when startup or shutdown hooks are required. See the FastAPI async testing guide.

Hypothesis does not automatically satisfy every Pydantic constraint or custom validator. Use explicit strategies for valid model inputs and separate cases that check validation failures.

The application already includes Hypothesis and Schemathesis fuzz tests in its normal member suite. See Learning platform tests for the generated properties, temporary-database isolation, larger test budgets, and seed-based reproduction commands. HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=fuzz just test services/app runs the service tests with up to 1,000 examples per property.

To fuzz the running local API at /v1/openapi.json:

uv run --group dev schemathesis run http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/openapi.json

Use a disposable test application and database: generated requests can create, change, and delete data. Service scaffolds provide /health/live and /health/ready; implement and start the application before running this command.

Testcontainers needs a running Docker daemon locally and in CI. Create and clean up containers in fixtures or context managers, and declare your application's chosen database driver with a version in the root manifest and an unversioned name in the member's dependencies. The PostgreSQL and Redis extras are included in the shared dev group. The app's integration fixtures start one PostgreSQL container per test session, using services.postgres.image from infra/docker-compose.yml as the single source for the database image. They create a separate schema for every test and Hypothesis example, apply migrations, and remove the schema after use. Unit tests run without Docker.

For local development, infra/docker-compose.yml provides persistent PostgreSQL and Redis services alongside Prometheus and Grafana. Add infra/docker-compose.dev.yml to run the API and migrations against that same PostgreSQL service. See infra/README.md for startup commands and connection settings. Testcontainers fixtures create their own disposable databases and can run independently of the development stack.

When using Colima, start it and point the Docker SDK at its socket before running integration tests:

colima start
export DOCKER_HOST="$(docker context inspect colima --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}')"
export TESTCONTAINERS_DOCKER_SOCKET_OVERRIDE=/var/run/docker.sock
just test services/app

Before running browser tests, install Chromium and start the application:

uv run --group dev python -m playwright install chromium

On Linux CI, use playwright install --with-deps chromium to install browser system dependencies too. For async browser fixtures, follow Playwright's async fixture setup, which requires the additional pytest-playwright-asyncio plugin and loop configuration. See Browser failure videos for the included sync fixtures' recording and Allure integration.

docs.title: Workspace tooling
docs.text:
Tool Purpose Availability / command uv Manage dependencies, the shared lockfile, and isolated environments. Install uv first; just bootstrap runs uv sync. Also declared in dev. Just Run the workspace's development commands. Install with uv tool install rust-just; run just to list recipes. Cookiecutter + Jinja2 Scaffold services and libraries and render the workspace README. dev; just new-service, just new-lib, just codegen. Ruff Lint and format Python code. dev; just lint, just format. pytest-cov + coverage.py Measure line and branch coverage and produce HTML, JSON, and XML reports per scope. dev; enabled by just test. allure-pytest Record test results and attachments for Allure reports. dev; enabled by just test. CI installs the Allure CLI separately to build reports. pre-commit Run repository hooks before commits. dev; enable with uv run pre-commit install. MkDocs + Material Build and serve the project's documentation. docs; just docs, just serve. Pants Infer member dependencies and select affected CI targets. Launcher installed separately; configured by pants.toml and member BUILD files.

See CI reports for report paths, publication, and history.
